textbookText: The power of a lens is measured in Dioptre (D) unit such that the focal length is expressed in metre. Therefore, power of a lens P = 1 D, its focal length f = 1m. For the combination of more than two lenses with equivalent power is an algebraic sum of powers of the individual lense which is given by, 111 P= f1 + f2 + f3 + ............ P = P1 + P2 + P3+ ............. A convex lens deviates the incident rays towards the axis and its power is taken positive while a concave lens deviates the incident rays away from the axis and its power is negative. If a convex lens and a concave lens of equal power are combined then, equivalent power of combination, p = p1 + (–p2) = p1 – p2 = 0 Therefore, the equivalent power will be zero for the combination of a convex lens and a concave lens both having equal power. It means the combination behaves as a glass plate.

17.8 Magnification Produced by a Lens Magnification is defined as the ratio between the dimensions of the image and the object. The process of magnification can occur in lenses, telescopes, microscopes, etc. Magnification produced by a lens depends on the position of objects. There are two types of magnification produced by a lens.
